blocks.passage:
A good short presentation has three parts: beginning, middle and end.

In the beginning, you say your name and your topic. In the middle, you share two or three main ideas. In the end, you give a conclusion and thank the audience.

Use simple words and clear sentences. Look at the audience. Speak slowly. A short, clear presentation is better than a long, confusing one.

items.q: What are the three parts of a good short presentation?
items.why: "A good short presentation has three parts: beginning, middle and end."

items.q: What do you say in the beginning?
items.why: "In the beginning, you say your name and your topic."

items.q: How many main ideas do you share in the middle?
items.why: "In the middle, you share two or three main ideas."

items.q: What do you do at the end?
options: Give a conclusion and thank the audience
items.why: "In the end, you give a conclusion and thank the audience."

items.q: According to the text, which is better?
items.why: "A short, clear presentation is better than a long, confusing one."

audio.text:
Good afternoon, everyone. My name is James, and today I'll talk about last quarter's sugar trade results. I'll be quick — about five minutes.

First, the beginning: my topic is simple. How did we do with sugar last quarter? In one sentence: it was a good quarter.

Now the middle — my three main ideas. One: sales went up eight percent compared with last year. Two: our costs stayed the same, so the profit grew. Three: we won two new clients in Brazil.

Let me repeat those three, because they matter. Sales up. Costs flat. Two new clients.

And now the end — my conclusion. It was a strong quarter for sugar, and the two new clients give us a good start for next quarter.

That's it. Short and clear. Thank you all for listening. Are there any questions?

See how it works? Name and topic, three ideas, one conclusion, thank you. You don't need more than that.

items.q: What is James's topic?
items.why: "today I'll talk about last quarter's sugar trade results."

items.q: In one sentence, how was the quarter?
items.why: "In one sentence: it was a good quarter."

items.q: What was the first main idea?
options: Sales went up eight percent compared with last year
items.why: "One: sales went up eight percent compared with last year."

items.q: What happened to costs?
options: They stayed the same, so profit grew
items.why: "Two: our costs stayed the same, so the profit grew."

items.q: What is the structure James recommends?
options: Name and topic, three ideas, one conclusion, thank you
items.why: "Name and topic, three ideas, one conclusion, thank you."

items.q: The **audience** is…
items.why: Audience = público.

items.q: A **conclusion** is…
options: the final part with the main message
items.why: Conclusion = conclusão.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "Share only two or three **___**."
items.why: Main idea = ideia principal.

items.q: To **introduce** yourself means to…
items.why: Introduce = apresentar-se.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "At the end, we **___** the audience."
items.why: Thank = agradecer.

items.q: "Let me **run through** the three ideas." To run through means to…
items.why: Run through = passar por, revisar.

items.q: "Sales **went up** eight percent." To go up means to…
items.why: Go up = subir.

items.q: "Costs **stayed the same**." To stay the same means to…
items.why: Stay the same = permanecer igual.

items.q: "I'll **be quick** — about five minutes." To be quick means to…
items.why: Be quick = ser breve.

items.q: "Any questions? **Fire away**." Fire away means…
items.why: Fire away = pode perguntar.
